# Architecture and code-health contract

## Structure (R04–R06)

Use a modular Rust application, not a rewrite and not a fleet of microservices.

```text
CLI / MCP / optional native transport
                  |
          eqm_application
       explicit use-case orchestration
          |                 |
  pure eqm_engine       host adapters
          |             manifest / store / trust / runner
       eqm_domain

Versioned protocol DTOs map boundary data to validated domain inputs.
```

`eqm_domain` owns validated values and local invariants. `eqm_engine` owns pure resolution, obligation derivation, semantic evaluation, comparison and deterministic explanations. `eqm_manifest` owns authored TOML/discovery/canonical projection and explicit conversion. `eqm_protocol` owns versioned JSON/SARIF and transport shapes; deserialization is not verification. `eqm_runner` owns authorized process supervision. `eqm_mcp` is a permission-limited adapter. The CLI package name is `eqm`, located in `crates/eqm_cli`.

Add `eqm_application` as the shared effectful use-case boundary. Initial planning allocation A01 places `authority`, `storage`, `trust`, `acquisition`, `evaluation`, and `query` modules inside it where appropriate. Split additional crates only when dependency isolation or privilege/packaging needs prove useful. These module names are navigation suggestions to be reconciled with actual code, not pre-existing symbols.

The application layer may orchestrate manifest/protocol/runner adapters, but it must not depend on CLI or MCP. Avoid a cycle where moving PreparedSession also moves its CLI-owned MCP-conversion helper into the application crate. Transport mapping stays outside the pure evaluator. No domain/engine dependency may introduce I/O implicitly.

## Two distinct operations (R05)

Acquisition is effectful: explicit source inspection, authorized worker execution, authorized import or permitted trust-material retrieval. Preparation captures the results into immutable validated input records. Evaluation is pure over that frozen input and an injected time value. Querying a stored evaluation is not acquisition. Missing inputs produce explicit non-success rather than secretly fetching or running tools.

Use narrow interfaces where external behavior changes: evidence reader/writer, signature verifier, authority loader, source snapshot provider, executor, time provider at the host boundary. Do not create a trait for every local struct. Avoid a universal manager with unrestricted access to all capabilities.

## Snapshot construction (R11, R22)

The engine's prepared input must have an enumerated required universe. A validated completeness boundary accounts for each coordinate as evaluated, explicitly not applicable, or unresolved. An immutable decision records that universe, exact input references, explanatory reasons and summary. Neither a public boolean nor deserializing an internal type may assert completeness, verified trust, or release authority.

A complete decision may contain failed, missing or unknown facts. The public API must preserve this distinction. Evaluation summaries are derived views, not mutable fields that callers can independently override.

## Code conventions (R50–R51)

Use validated newtypes for IDs, digest domains, revisions, subjects and counts. Prefer explicit enums/state machines for lifecycle distinctions and typed contextual errors with sources and machine codes. Avoid large constructor argument lists by validated parameter objects when they improve correctness. Do not use stringly typed truth, status, trust or scope values in domain logic.

Keep inputs and decisions immutable; share read-only data rather than repeatedly cloning entire graphs. Preserve deterministic ordering. No ambient current directory, environment inheritance, global mutable state, implicit network access, hidden runtime, or internal SystemTime reads in pure evaluation.

Retain the repo's panic/unwrap/expect/unsafe restrictions in production. Tests may use repository-approved patterns, but test conveniences must not enter production factories or features. Do not add Default/Deserialize/public field escape hatches to completeness, trust, or authorization types. Newtypes and private constructors prevent accidents, not malicious code with equal process privilege.

Keep the pure core unsafe-free. Any unavoidable native/OS bridge must be narrowly isolated and documented, with safe external wrappers considered first. Update repository instructions and lint scopes explicitly before introducing an exception; never remove the workspace unsafe rule globally. A process boundary, not catch_unwind, provides crash isolation when required.

## Concurrency and lifecycle

Pure evaluation remains independently callable without an async runtime. Host I/O may be asynchronous where actual integration warrants it; do not mandate an unchosen runtime. Tasks have owners, bounded queues, explicit cancellation, and shutdown joining/cleanup. Do not detach background work that can outlive authority or expose half-published results. Capture publication/commit semantics for cancellation races rather than guessing them from timing.

## Incremental migration of the implementation

Create validated internal primitives and fixtures before routing production entry points. Replace duplicated CLI decision paths with the application service one command at a time. Keep the existing fail-closed release path until the new protected pipeline is fully connected. Remove old evaluators after equivalence/regression tests, not before. Do not maintain alternate production truth calculators behind convenience flags.

Feature flags, if needed, isolate optional host capabilities and native packaging. They never disable validation or turn absent security functionality into pass. Enumerate actual supported combinations and test them; do not invent a broad feature matrix before inspecting Cargo manifests.

# Compatibility, schemas and migration contract

## Four version axes (R21, R52)

Version the public wire schemas, evaluation semantics, optional native ABI, and database schema independently. `eqm_product_v1` is this specification's name; it is not permission to repurpose existing `schemas/v1` URLs with incompatible semantics. Tool/package version is another implementation identity used for reproducibility.

The baseline repository explicitly supports current-only v1, prohibits legacy readers/aliases, and generates schemas from DTOs. Preserve that public contract until the compatibility decision step records an explicit policy. Do not introduce invisible fallback readers merely to keep a fixture passing. Repository proof that no public legacy compatibility is required may permit a coordinated version transition, but it must be documented.

## Version decision gate

Before new incompatible wire shapes are exposed, inspect actual published releases, consumers, schema generators/URI checks and declared support obligations. Record the chosen new namespace/version or coordinated pre-release transition and corresponding exact tests. Do not select a magic version number from this package. Human approval is required when a choice changes externally committed compatibility or product scope.

Exact JSON field names, optionality, integer ranges, timestamp precision, extension semantics and digest domains are closed in this decision and accompanying protocol spec. Unknown security-critical semantics fail closed. Reader compatibility, where explicitly supported, is tested; unsupported versions produce clear errors rather than implicit reinterpretation.

## Signed records

Retain original exact bytes and signature material. Migration creates new records with explicit source/provenance, never rewrites an original while claiming its signature covers changed data. Historical replay may require the original evaluator/runtime in a controlled environment; an unsupported version is a stated limitation, not a reason to promote results under new semantics automatically.

## Database transitions

Migrations execute under exclusive coordination with safe interruption/recovery and backups appropriate to the selected storage guarantees. Version checks prevent incompatible concurrent writers. Test upgrade, interruption, reopen, rollback or restore, and unavailable older/newer readers. Schema migration does not silently destroy immutable objects/receipts or release archives. Retention cleanup is a separate authorized lifecycle.

## Distribution

Exact dependencies and toolchain pins remain justified and locked. Audit the actual linked SQLite and cryptographic implementation and the included native libraries. Keep generated artifacts out of source except intentional generated schemas/approved bindings. Preserve reproducible distribution verification, checksums, SPDX/SBOM inputs and provenance. Local unsigned distribution is not publication/signing authorization.

Native/sidecar consumers negotiate compatibility and fail explicitly when unsupported. UI/report consumers show unsupported statuses instead of assuming success. Support matrices are owner-approved and backed by host execution, not merely cross-compilation.

## Revision 2 owner-approved direction

ADR-0012 resolves the direction in Q03: incompatible changes use an explicit new namespace; preserve signed originals, reject unsupported versions and avoid implicit fallback readers. S006 still determines exact namespace/URI spelling, numeric/time/null/set representations and the consumer transition from inspected evidence. No known external consumer obligation may be silently discarded; document a newly discovered conflict before exposure. Wire/evaluator/database/optional-ABI versions remain independent.

The approved initial EQM execution/storage host targets are macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64. They are verification obligations, not completed host certifications. Product participant OS/SDK/cohort promises remain separate unresolved facts. No N/N-1 cohort or Windows support is inferred.

# Logical data model

These are semantic record contracts, not finalized Rust declarations, table DDL, JSON schemas, field spellings, or new CLI flags. Finalize exact representations in the referenced implementation steps after inspecting the existing types. Do not infer a new product backend schema from this model.

## Existing authority to preserve

Capabilities group product value. Journeys order surfaces/transitions. Surfaces own requirements and reusable fragments expand through exact pins. Bindings associate shared units with native artifacts and evidence selectors. Policy/profile selections determine obligations. Retain validated identities, risk/lifecycle invariants, owners, explicit extensions and deterministic maps.

## Target and participant records (R07–R09, R13)

| Logical record | Required meaning and validation |
|---|---|
| Product role | An authored role such as edge/control tower/CLI/provider; it is not a platform enum that forces all product behavior. |
| Shipped target | Stable identity of an independently released output with platform/architecture/configuration metadata when relevant. |
| Source component | Repository-confined source ownership plus explicit shared-source dependencies; shared KMP source sets may contribute to many outputs. |
| Capability participation | Approved requirement/target/profile applicability, with explicit false versus unresolved status. |
| Scenario participant | A role-bearing occurrence within a scenario; two devices of the same target remain distinct actors. |
| Subject manifest | Exact participant-to-build/artifact/source/configuration assignments, including providers/deployments where required. |
| Comparison context | Shared contract/scenario/logical-profile/comparison-rule identity, separate from the distinct participant subjects. |

Provider obligations bind exact provider identity/configuration, not every target indiscriminately without an explicit dependency mapping. Shared-provider and end-to-end evidence cannot be satisfied by duplicate per-target passes. Product-supported version combinations are approved data, not a hardcoded N/N-1 promise.

## Evaluation records (R11, R14, R19)

An obligation coordinate includes selected policy and revision, complete selected profile revisions/values, unit, fully qualified requirement, scope/participant subject, facet, and appropriate immutable candidate/context identity. Strength includes the constraints applicable to that coordinate: required level, accepted evidence/trust requirements, maximum age and count semantics. Public obligation IDs must bind the complete coordinate, not omit profile/release context.

A required-universe record enumerates obligations and explicit not-applicable/unresolved coordinates, expected selection manifests, and protected scope. A prepared evaluation contains that universe, exact inputs and verification conclusions. An evaluation decision contains statuses, all reasons, completeness, scope, evidence acceptance/rejection, exposure comparisons, applied waivers, conformance/comparison summaries and input/evaluator/time identities.

Display labels and file locations remain provenance rather than semantic identity, unless a path is itself a declared behavioral/build input. Use projections deliberately; do not treat every path as globally irrelevant.

## Evidence lifecycle records (R16–R20)

Raw object: original exact bytes with raw content digest, retained according to class. Normalized evidence: schema-specific semantic assertion with its own digest. Execution identity: authorized plan/campaign/run/logical selection/attempt identity. A verification receipt binds raw/semantic subject relationships and verifier/trust context without acting as an unforgeable serialized capability.

An expected selection manifest defines the cases/observations meant to run. An execution receipt accounts for selected outcomes and terminal worker state, including skips, filters, quarantine, timeout, cancellation and malformed result failures. Retry relationships reference the same logical case rather than producing additional minimum-count credit.

A campaign identifies an authorized evaluation/acquisition grouping for an exact subject and selection. Campaign-selection and supersession rules are explicit; producer-controlled observation time is not sole ordering authority. History remains immutable even when a later campaign becomes the current selected one.

A stored import associates raw object identity, semantic evidence identity, execution identity and verification metadata. Duplicate delivery is idempotent. Contradictory authenticated payloads for one immutable attempt become a conflict record. Unrelated rejected evidence must not accidentally poison an otherwise complete scope; relevant malformed/conflicting inputs remain visible and non-authorizing.

## Authority and release records (R23–R29, R63)

Protected authority includes baseline contract/policy/participation/selection/evidence mapping/waiver/trust/evaluator identities. Trust configuration defines authorized identities/issuers/builders, algorithms, required material and temporal constraints. Exact operational values require owner configuration.

Candidate readiness is distinct from a post-deployment observation. A decision can be signed whether it passes or fails. A release authorization references the accepted exact decision, artifact/participant set, destination/channel, explicit allowed deviations, authority and validity. Deployment consumption checks those bindings; it does not execute deployments itself. A deployment receipt records what was actually promoted and supports later conformance evaluation.

No record's identity may depend on a descendant that references it. A decision cannot be part of the input evidence identity needed to construct itself.

## Storage and migrations

Objects are immutable; the local transactional index contains discoverable references and derived query indexes. It cannot mint trust. Persist enough manifests and provenance to reconstruct decisions and recover indexes. Database migration versions are independent of wire/evaluator/ABI versions. Retain original signed payloads through conversions and explicit migrations. See COMPATIBILITY.md for the version decision gate.

## Approved validated-state and observation closure

RA05/RA06 require finalization and prepared completeness to be constructed only after expansion, inherited-risk validation and complete-coordinate accounting. Public hidden constructors and deserialization must not bypass these boundaries; retain pure acyclic crate dependencies when allocating ownership.

Exact raw bytes, semantic assertions and immutable attempts remain separate identities (RA08/RA15). Duplicated delivery preserves provenance without count inflation; same-attempt conflicts remain durable and relevant to their coordinates. RA13 requires one strict envelope/payload/subject/kind/reference/time conversion before admission. Parsing is not verification.

Observed role/inventory/exposure facts are independently obtained for an independently expected subject; copied authored declarations or a document's presence are insufficient (RA21). Waivers bind exact policy/profile revisions, subject and context and enumerate only actual contributions (RA09).

# Normative evaluation semantics

This contract is the basis for a small reference evaluator and golden/property tests. Centralization is not permission to bless every current engine behavior. Compare existing functions and tests, document ambiguous policy semantics, and resolve them explicitly before wiring production.

## Evaluation order and completeness (R08, R11–R15, R58)

First validate schema/local invariants and resolve protected or development authority appropriate to mode. Select exact policy/profile revisions and values; reject duplicate requests and out-of-policy values. Protected modes cannot use candidate-local defaults.

Enumerate the required target/provider/scenario universe before evidence selection. Applicability is evaluated at the appropriate requirement/participant/profile coordinate. Explicit false under approved authority may be non-applicable. Unknown stays in the visible universe and is non-authorizing. Missing profile context cannot make a requirement disappear. Empty release scopes require protected explicit permission; otherwise no release authorization. A one-member cohort does not support a meaningful cross-target equivalence claim.

Derive scope- and facet-specific constraints. Compose relevant matching policy rules monotonically: stronger minimum trust/count and tighter age constrain rather than weaken. Do not accidentally apply one facet's unrelated rule to another. Whether selectors express required conjunctions or approved alternatives must be explicit and tested; do not invent an OR interpretation to obtain a pass.

Then map evidence by exact semantic subject, specification, binding, contract, profiles, execution and release/candidate context; verify trust independently; evaluate temporal eligibility and attempt/count semantics; perform actual structure/inventory/exposure checks; apply only authorized waivers; aggregate complete target/provider/scenario results and contract-relative comparison conclusions.

## Facet states and precedence

Preserve the current canonical distinction among NotApplicable, Satisfied, Waived, Failed, Stale, Missing, Unstable and Unknown. Do not infer ordering from enum discriminants. The baseline pure facet evaluator uses: explicit inapplicability first; unknown applicability/context/coverage/outcome/freshness/trust/supporting facts next; unstable history next; failure, stale, then missing; otherwise satisfied. Preserve all contributing reasons even when one summary state takes precedence. A conflicting immutable identity can make coverage unknown; unstable retry history is separately visible.

The baseline permits a valid waiver over failed/stale/missing provisional states, not over unknown/unstable states. Preserve that fail-closed boundary unless a separately reviewed contract change defines something stricter or otherwise explicit. A waiver is not a successful evidence outcome. Insufficient known trust and unknown verification are distinguishable, but neither satisfies an obligation.

Every supported payload must have explicit evaluation: tests, structural checks, snapshots, inventories, runtime snapshots, manual review and release-related evidence. A catch-all payload arm returning success is prohibited. A failed manual review, quarantined selection, missing expected case, zero selected cases, retry failure, timeout, and cancellation all have explicit non-success effects.

## Counts and campaigns (R16–R18)

Count the declared logical units, not files, imported copies or attempts. Bind the expected selection manifest to the plan/campaign. A threshold is applied to the required coordinate using policy-composed constraints; acquisition may report a successful execution without claiming policy satisfaction. Minimum-count semantics for different evidence kinds must be closed before exposing those kinds as acceptable; a release-record reference cannot automatically satisfy an arbitrary observation count.

Within a campaign, preserve immutable attempt history. Duplicate transport never changes aggregate counts. Contradictory results for the same immutable attempt are a conflict. A later passing retry does not erase earlier failing history. Across campaigns, explicit authorized selection determines current eligibility while old results remain available for audit. No arbitrary latest timestamp and no permanent failure poisoning from unrelated superseded campaigns.

## Supporting checks (R28, R59)

A file's declared role is not an observed role. Structural success requires the needed independent observation, correct type/confinement, and valid role evidence. Trusted complete current inventory can prove absence; partial, missing or untrusted inventory remains unknown. Presence of a runtime-facts document is not exposure match: compare its actual facts to authored expectations for the same exact subject/profile/time.

## Aggregates and reporting

Aggregate complete participating target/provider/scenario obligations. A target cannot ignore its provider or end-to-end dependencies. Missing participant evaluations yield unknown comparison, not a reduced target cohort. Extraneous targets are visible but do not change the protected required set. Relational checks compare specified normalized outcomes from the same scenario; separate target passes do not replace them.

Satisfied and explicitly not-applicable facets can form conformance; valid applied waivers may form conditional conformance; blocking states remain nonconformant or unknown as defined by the normative table. Release authorization rejects unknown and requires explicit protected treatment of conditional outcomes. Do not force all interfaces into the same display word if their objects differ, but ensure they reference one decision and never contradict its facts.

Filters, pagination, truncation and resource limits are presentation/execution concerns. They cannot modify the completeness denominator, required cohort, selected campaign, or release conclusion. A resource limit preventing complete evaluation must be explicit and non-authorizing.

## Properties required in tests

Permuting semantically unordered inputs leaves results stable. Duplicate delivery leaves results stable. Changing any bound subject/authority/profile/executable/evidence component prevents inappropriate reuse. Removing required evidence cannot strengthen a decision. Weakening candidate authority cannot weaken protected requirements. Adding irrelevant rejected records cannot manufacture a pass. Reference and optimized evaluation agree for the same frozen input. Time and trust changes affect current acceptance without mutating historical decisions.

## Approved precise semantics — ADR-0012

The owner approved the following closure rules; RA01–RA09 and RA21 carry executable regression obligations.

Required expected-selection members compose with AND. Alternative groups exist only when explicitly authorized by policy and bound into the frozen selection; observed pass/fail results cannot opportunistically select a different alternative. First account for all required cases, then apply the coordinate's count threshold to distinct eligible logical units. Enough passing observations cannot hide a required failing or missing case.

For schema-valid eligible evidence, separate required cases containing fail/pass aggregate to Failed. Fail/pass retries of the same logical case within the selected campaign aggregate to Unstable. Contradictory assertions for the same immutable attempt create Unknown conflict. Malformed count/outcome relationships reject admission and leave affected required evidence unresolved. Timeout/cancellation remains Unknown; skip/filter/quarantine/missing remains non-success. Existing facet precedence and contributing reasons still apply after these outcome calculations.

Count units must be declared per kind: expected logical test cases; independently checked structural/inventory/runtime facts; explicit review slots and authorized distinct principals where independence is required; or an exact eligible independently verified referenced record. One release-record reference provides at most one eligible record unit and cannot meet an arbitrary minimum. Repeated files/transports/attempts never increase credit. Fixture thresholds are synthetic; real policy supplies validated minimums, maximum ages, skew and allowed deviations.

Campaign eligibility is an explicit authorized selection bound to the decision. Supersession is an explicit trusted relationship; neither latest timestamps nor unrelated old campaigns determine current acceptance. Keep all historical attempts for audit.

Policy strengthening compares inclusion of the protected required universe plus constraints for corresponding coordinates. Increasing `minimum_level` can remove obligations and must not be treated as automatically stronger. Compose trust/count/age only from the rules matching each facet. Exact policy/profile revisions and context remain part of the coordinate.

Expanded fragment requirements inherit the stronger fragment-default and destination-journey risk. Absence inherits that value; explicit risk below it rejects. Validate the expanded graph before finalized/prepared construction. Preserve this rule through canonical projection and real manifest loading; see DEV-001.

Freshness uses explicit evaluation time and policy, preserving exact nanosecond arithmetic rather than flooring to milliseconds. Freeze supported canonical forms and all equality/expiry/skew boundary vectors in S006/S069. Do not inherit an undocumented fixed skew as production policy.

# Evidence, identity and reproducibility

## Binding semantics (R18–R22)

Use separate domain-separated semantic digest projections for contracts, bindings, evidence specifications, target configuration, runners, adapters, policy/profile selection, authority and trust configuration. Hashing only a binding/specification ID pair is insufficient. The workspace digest remains a useful summary, not a replacement for each component's meaning.

A runner identity used in evidence must include the approved executable content as well as its definition and relevant execution/toolchain context. A wrapper script hash alone does not establish the identity of mutable code or toolchains it invokes. Record the inputs necessary for the claim's threat model rather than asserting universal hermeticity. Immutable trusted source snapshots differ from local dirty-tree development provenance.

Three identities must coexist: raw object bytes, normalized semantic evidence, and authorized execution/attempt. Original signed bytes remain available for verification. Transport formatting changes can yield a different raw object without a different semantic assertion. Reimporting an identical assertion/attempt is idempotent and cannot increase counts. Two conflicting accepted assertions for one immutable attempt form a persistent conflict, not last-writer-wins.

Canonical serialization is a protocol specification, not the default serializer output. RFC 8785 is the approved direction: reject duplicate JSON names, preserve Unicode string data, distinguish semantic sets from ordered sequences, and specify numeric/time/null behavior. Exact field ranges/representations must be frozen with cross-runtime test vectors before schema publication. Do not silently normalize signed bytes. Source path portability normalization is a separate concern from JCS string preservation.

## Campaign and selection contract (R16–R17)

An authorized plan names exact selectors and an expected inventory of logical cases/observations. A campaign groups executions for that subject/selection. Each logical case has explicit attempts, terminal outcomes, and provenance. Missing selections remain missing even when reported cases all pass. File count and retry count are not observation count.

Selection of a current campaign is an explicit policy choice with approved ordering/supersession authority. It is not arbitrary timestamp max, directory sort order, or the one run the caller happens to supply. Local exploration can display selected subsets but cannot claim complete release assurance from them. Maintain audit/reliability history without allowing irrelevant past failures to permanently poison future authorized campaigns.

## Acyclic lifecycle (R20)

```text
protected authority + candidate subject manifest
                       |
             approved plan / campaign
                       |
  evidence + worker receipts + available runtime observations
                       |
              frozen input manifest
                       |
               evaluation decision
                       |
            signed statement (optional)
                       |
         protected release authorization
                       |
           deployment receipt / observations
```

References point to records already defined. Evidence binds a plan/candidate subject, not the future decision that includes the evidence. Post-deployment observations feed a later evaluation, not a circular initial-readiness prerequisite. Do not reuse the old release-record field mechanically where it introduces such a cycle.

## Input freezing

Use one consistent authority/evidence/index generation when creating an input manifest. Capture clock and trust context explicitly. A snapshot stores required scope, selected campaigns, subject mappings, exact referenced objects and verification material. Missing objects invalidate preparation; concurrent imports cannot silently change an in-progress decision.

For local development, expose dirty/untracked source identity and confidence. For trusted evaluation, bind what actually executed to the authorized immutable source/build inputs. Never label execution of modified bytes as clean HEAD.

## Import and collision handling

Validate byte bounds and syntax before normalization. Verify semantic digests and identity/subject relationships. Classify duplicate delivery, semantically identical alternate transport, and contradictory immutable attempt independently. Persist receipt/provenance relationships transactionally with the evidence index. A malicious unrelated file should be rejected without silently replacing a valid result; a conflict relevant to required scope must remain visible and non-authorizing.

The database/index is not a source of trust. Imported statements that claim verified state cross the verification boundary again. Rebuilt indexes preserve identities and conflicts; they must not fabricate new successful verification receipts.

FILE: specs/EXECUTION_SECURITY.md

# Acquisition, filesystem, process and transport security

## Explicit authorization (R30–R34)

A dry-run resolves every selected executable and digest, typed argv, selector/case selection, cwd, explicit environment/secret references, backend capabilities, time/output/resource/concurrency limits and output destination. It performs bounded approved reads but no execution, including no executable discovery. A plan identity binds subsequent approval. Any meaningful plan change invalidates approval; secret values never appear in the plan.

Execute direct argv, not shell command strings or ambiguous command interpolation. A repository-owned script can still execute arbitrary code; direct argv is not a sandbox. Execution authority is provided by the operator/host, not synthesized from candidate declarations of enforceable guarantees. Validate actual backend capabilities and reject unsupported guarantees.

Worker mounts/permissions prevent access to evaluator/authority mutation, durable evidence database writes, signing credentials and unrelated product/user data. Provide a dedicated output/staging area. Discovery that executes Gradle or another program is subject to the same rules. Hostile contribution builds may need disposable isolated workers; process groups and ordinary containers do not automatically establish every threat-model guarantee. Document supported isolation rather than pretending all hosts are equivalent.

## Complete process supervision (R32)

The deadline covers spawn, execution, descendants, stdout/stderr drainage, result-file acquisition and cleanup. Immediate-child exit is not the end of supervision. Readers signal overflow promptly; stop workers on overflow/cancellation/deadline and drain only within bounded shutdown. Reap owned children and clean staged outputs on every error path. Signal child trees using platform-appropriate ownership (including Windows Job Objects when Windows is supported), not only the direct child. Detached/escaped processes require explicit host containment rather than optimistic cleanup claims.

Define terminal precedence for simultaneous overflow/timeout/cancellation and retain all reasons. Success requires valid terminal execution and normalized output, not just exit zero. Persist failure/timeout/cancel receipts where safely possible so required work does not vanish. A result already atomically committed before cancellation remains discoverable; cancellation must not rewrite committed success or create a phantom completed record. Exact API cancellation semantics are frozen in tests before exposure.

## Filesystem and byte boundaries (R33)

Perform confinement through safe opened handles/capability boundaries where available; lexical checks and final-component symlink checks alone are insufficient. Validate ancestors, final type, containment and limits. Address TOCTOU by retaining validated handles rather than validate-then-reopen where possible. Trusted execution uses immutable materialized inputs. Tests must cover parent symlinks, replacement races, path aliases/collisions and output files changed after child exit.

Enforce size before unbounded allocation. A result-file cap applies at read time, not only in a parser after fs::read. Bound existing collision files, imported evidence, attachments and logs. Validate digest and regular-file requirements after execution, do not assume a pre-created temp filename remained safe. Independently observe structural roles; never populate observed roles from authored declarations merely to make comparison pass.

## Environment and secrets

Clear ambient environment; provide an operator-authorized host PATH and explicitly declared inputs, not a hardcoded Unix PATH on all systems. Resolve secret references through an explicit provider. Redact retained outputs and structured errors with bounded behavior, but do not claim redaction stops a malicious authorized process exfiltrating secrets. Avoid giving untrusted workers secrets at all. Logging, plans, reports and test fixtures must not include production credentials.

## Resource limits (R42)

Bound parser bytes/depth, graph/fragment expansion, profile combinations, candidate evidence, attachment sizes, queue lengths, worker concurrency and requests. Exact budgets are configured and benchmarked; this conversation did not approve arbitrary numeric values. Limits must fail explicitly and non-authorizing, never silently truncate the required universe. Preserve deterministic ordering under bounded concurrency.

## MCP and consumer transport (R47)

MCP is read-only by default and reads prepared snapshots. Text/descriptions/logs/attachments remain untrusted data and cannot become instructions, runner approval, signer selection or waiver authority. Use private stdio or restricted authenticated IPC; do not add an unauthenticated localhost HTTP daemon by default. Bound requests/responses and show pagination/truncation truthfully. Mutating/executing/signing capabilities need separate explicit authorization and must not be inferred from read permissions.

## Security tests

Use adversarial fake workers and disposable fixture roots: inherited environment, shell metacharacters as one arg, parent symlink, bounded large result, flooding streams, immediate parent exit with open descendant pipes, cancellation races, malformed payload, missing expected selection, replay/conflict, unsupported backend guarantee and attempted authority-store writes. Run native host tests rather than treating cross-compilation as evidence of process isolation or durability.

## Approved lifecycle and host closure

Initial EQM host targets are macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 (ADR-0012). Product mobile/desktop targets are separately discovered. Unsupported hosts reject guarantees they cannot provide; Windows support is not implied. Native tests on each declared host remain required before claiming support.

RA11 extends whole-invocation supervision explicitly to stdin: establish deadline/cancellation and cleanup ownership before request delivery, handle backpressure concurrently with output, and retain child ownership on broken pipes. Child exit does not end input/output/descendant cleanup supervision. Test all lifecycle stages, not only retained output size.

RA12 applies bounded regular-file handle and confinement rules to every ingress, including config/lock files, executable reads and existing-object comparisons. Test FIFO/device inputs, ancestor symlinks, replacement and growth races; do not allocate the full file before checking its budget or create work directories before validating confinement. Actual isolation/network/secrets and resource ceilings remain independent operator configuration, not worker declarations.

# Product specification — eqm_product_v1

Status: approved intent. Requirement IDs R01–R64 are stable traceability keys, not wire-schema versions. `eqm_product_v1` names this product specification; it does not authorize silently changing `schemas/v1` semantics.

## Purpose and users (R01–R03, R10)

EquivalenceMatrix is a local-first graph of shared product contracts, target-specific bindings, policy/profiles, independently produced evidence, and deterministic conformance/equivalence decisions. Developers, test/release engineers, and authorized operators use it to identify missing work and establish appropriately scoped assurance. It is not a source generator and does not require native targets to share implementations.

The user's product has a Rust command-line application, a Kotlin Multiplatform desktop control tower where users view account/task state and review workflows, and a Kotlin Multiplatform mobile edge application where users add/edit business evidence using photo/video/voice and related annotations. Relevant backend/shared providers participate where cross-runtime contracts depend on them. Exact operating systems, supported versions, source repositories, product API routes, and business rules were not supplied.

Business evidence belongs to the product's authorization, storage, revision and synchronization domain. Conformance evidence belongs to EQM. Do not store raw user media in the conformance engine or treat a content hash as proof of a real-world assertion. A user account ID or task ID in a synthetic scenario is not a new EQM account/task data model.

## Required capabilities

Preserve stable semantic IDs for capabilities, journeys, surfaces, requirements, fragments, targets, bindings, policies, profiles, evidence selectors, runners, adapters, and approved waivers. Resolve and validate authored authority; reject duplicate identities, invalid references, weakened protected scope, invalid fragment pins, and unsupported schemas. Derive exact obligations, acquire/import evidence only under explicit permission, and evaluate completeness, coverage, trust, freshness, attempts, inventory and exposure without hidden execution.

Make every conclusion explainable through an immutable input manifest and a complete evaluated snapshot. CLI checks, matrices, MCP, context, release checks and statements must display the same underlying conclusions. Efficient selective views may omit display rows, never required evaluation scope.

Support deliberate target asymmetry. Shared business invariants may apply broadly; camera capture may apply only to mobile; bulk review may apply only to desktop; synchronization scenarios span roles. A permanent design difference is modeled as approved participation, not an exception waiver.

## Claim boundaries

“Conformant” means the exact subject satisfies the declared obligations in the selected authority and profile context. “Equivalent” means contract-relative equivalence within a declared comparison cohort; it is not proof of universal program equivalence. Where output agreement is required, evidence must include a relational check over the same scenario and approved normalization rules. A screenshot or two independent target passes do not satisfy a separately required cross-target scenario.

Complete evaluation is not successful evaluation. Unknown, missing, stale, failed, unstable, insufficient trust, and waived evidence remain explicit. Signing an accurate failure record does not make it successful. Promotion requires separate protected release authorization for the exact artifact set and destination.

## Workflows (R44, R48, R60)

Development: inspect/validate authority; select exact scope; inspect a fully resolved dry-run plan; authorize acquisition separately; persist immutable normalized evidence and receipts; evaluate frozen inputs; inspect findings; rerun only justified affected work. A runner's zero exit is an acquisition result, not product conformance.

Pull request: use trusted invocation/protected baseline as required; compare candidate changes including deletions; evaluate candidate implementations against protected expectations; conservatively expand unknown changed dependencies; never execute candidate-controlled grading or signing authority as trusted infrastructure.

Release readiness: select protected authority and a candidate subject manifest, complete all required target/provider/scenario obligations, verify every mandatory input, decide readiness, optionally sign the decision, and separately authorize promotion. Post-deployment conformance uses observations that exist after deployment; it cannot be a circular prerequisite for the first deployment.

Product integration: adopt one real capture/edit/sync/review/export slice before multiplying features. Bind real native test selections, runtime observations and build outputs. Synthetic fixtures establish EQM semantics, not actual product readiness.

## Non-goals and conditional work

No EQM business backend, UI framework, feature-flag service, cloud orchestration platform, standalone deployment system, full Kotlin reimplementation, mandatory sidecar, or mandatory mobile evaluator. No authorization to publish, deploy, select live signers, or alter other product repositories is implied by approval of this spec. Native embedding is documented as an optional gated extension, not added to the default runtime surface.

## Success and rollout

A successful implementation closes the static-review gaps, satisfies the acceptance catalog, passes the relevant supported-host and native lanes, and makes all production guarantees evidence-backed. Start release gating in shadow mode, independently review decisions, then require explicit approval to enforce. Rollback uses a known-good evaluator or pauses promotion; it never becomes permissive.

# Rust and Kotlin Multiplatform integration

## Required scope (R01–R03, R07–R10, R48)

Initial EQM runs in developer tooling and CI. The Rust product CLI and the desktop/mobile KMP apps are targets under test. Test adapters and selected runtime observation producers bridge native tools to EQM's normalized evidence. These adapters do not make the business app depend on EQM's internal crates.

Actual product repositories, build tasks, platform minimums, desktop JVM/native choice, device matrix, provider APIs and compatibility windows were not supplied. Discover them read-only where accessible and record them before implementing real adapters. Repository-local synthetic fixtures are appropriate for validating EQM, but cannot be labeled proof of actual mobile persistence/sync behavior.

Rust: link the shared EQM application service into EQM's own CLI. A product CLI needs a direct Rust dependency only for an actual local conformance feature; otherwise use it as a producer/consumer in test tooling. Keep EQM's package/binary distinct from the product's CLI.

KMP: represent shared source sets separately from shipped target outputs. `commonMain` changes invalidate all dependent outputs. Native tests retain their frameworks and explicit selectors. Adapter discovery is not permission to execute build scripts. Result normalization binds exact build/selection/attempt IDs and expected inventory; missing cases cannot vanish.

## Product contracts to author first

Shared invariants: correct account/task association, authorization boundaries, valid transitions, evidence revision identity and operation idempotency. Mobile-specific contracts: offline durable capture, interrupted photo/video/voice workflows, permission denial, editable annotations/revisions and resumable/recoverable uploads. Desktop-specific contracts: correct projections, visible stale/offline state, review history, conflict visibility and paginated large-account views. CLI contracts: inspection/export/automation behavior actually supported by the product. Cross-runtime scenarios link these roles and providers.

These are acceptance themes approved in the conversation, not invented endpoint names, storage models, UI designs, conflict algorithms or legal guarantees. The product owner must define the exact conflict, deletion, authorization and supported-format rules; EQM can then test them.

## Canonical first scenario

1. With synthetic authorized account/task fixtures, capture business evidence offline on mobile.
2. Edit the approved annotation/revision metadata; terminate the application after a save acknowledgment.
3. Restart and verify the acknowledged state survives.
4. Reconnect and retry interrupted synchronization.
5. Verify desktop reviews the intended revision exactly once under the correct task.
6. Verify CLI inspection/export observes the same approved logical revision.
7. Assert no duplicate logical record, cross-account disclosure or silent loss of acknowledged state.

Extend with account switching, permission revocation, concurrent edits, interrupted uploads, stale projections, backend upgrades and older supported clients. Do not promise a particular consistency algorithm; the contract specifies permitted offline observations and post-reconciliation invariants.

## Optional native embedding (R49)

Only activate for an explicitly required local evaluation feature. A desktop sidecar is a valid option for interactive local use or fault containment, not an automatic daemon. A read-only versioned report consumer may suffice. If a sidecar is chosen, use restricted IPC, version negotiation, bounded messages, cancellation and lifecycle ownership; no unauthenticated localhost default and no per-row process spawn.

If an in-process bridge is chosen, define a small Kotlin-facing abstraction and platform-specific implementations. UniFFI's documented Kotlin path uses JNA; it is not automatically a Kotlin/Native iOS implementation. Kotlin/Native C interop is an alternative boundary to evaluate. Select one coherent strategy with a demonstrated cross-platform slice, not multiple experimental bridges.

The bridge contract covers explicit allocation/free ownership, closed handles, cancellation/completion races, safe threading, errors, batch APIs, numeric/time mapping, supported ABI versions and bounded inputs. Never expose Rust memory layouts/collections over a stable ABI. Keep unsafe code isolated and reviewed; catch_unwind is not isolation from aborting panics. Product capture/media payloads stay in product/platform code, not large buffers through EQM evaluation APIs.

The optional sequence is in implementation/OPTIONAL_NATIVE_COMMIT_SEQUENCE.md. Do not mark it complete or activate it simply because the mandatory EQM core is approved.

# Persistence, lifecycle and performance

## Storage model (R35–R37)

Use immutable content-addressed objects and a transactional local metadata/index store. The approved initial index direction is SQLite. Keep trusted release storage outside candidate-writable mounts; development `.eqm/` remains ignored generated state. Do not assume a developer-owned directory is a hostile-worker security boundary.

Publication protocol: write/validate in protected staging; durably install the immutable object; commit the index transaction referencing installed objects; expose the committed record. A crash before indexing can leave an orphan. A visible completed record must never reference bytes that were not safely published. Test the actual file/directory durability guarantees on supported OS/filesystem combinations.

Handle concurrent directory initialization, duplicate installation, transaction contention and idempotency. Distinguish raw-object collision, equivalent semantic transport and conflicting attempt identity. Immutable objects do not prevent legitimate extra raw encodings, nor permit contradictory attempts to overwrite one another.

Store enough immutable manifests/receipts and metadata to rebuild indexes without minting trust or losing conflicts. Validate referenced objects when reopening/replaying. A missing or corrupt object produces a bounded explicit unavailable result, not fabricated history. Use short read snapshots for coherent decisions; avoid long-lived transactions across native test execution.

## SQLite operational contract (R36)

Pin and audit an implementation containing SQLite's documented WAL-reset corruption fix. The upstream fix is in 3.51.3 and later or documented backports; this is a fix floor, not an instruction to pin that old release forever. Verify the actually linked runtime, not only a wrapper crate's version. WAL is for a local host, not network-filesystem or cross-device synchronization. One writer at a time requires bounded contention handling and explicit checkpoint ownership. Decide/test durability settings, transaction atomicity, busy behavior, crash recovery and backups.

Configuration/version evidence belongs in the implementation ADR and build reports. Current library/feature names and pin versions must be discovered and audited before dependency commits, with explicit lockfile changes.

## Retention and GC (R37)

Define classes for temporary local work, long-lived release evidence, original signed payloads, verification material, logs and attachments. Exact periods require owner policy. Immutable does not mean retain forever. GC respects running acquisitions, active readers, snapshots, archive references and release decisions; use reachability/leases appropriate to the store and test races. Reclaim orphan staging only after proving it is not live.

Prefer synthetic product data for conformance tests. Restrict sensitive attachments/log access and do not put actual business media or account secrets into public fixtures. Encryption/access policies are an operator decision, not an unapproved cryptographic subsystem to invent in this module.

## Historical replay versus current acceptance (R38)

Replay uses original input/evaluator/trust/time identities to reproduce the historical decision. Current acceptance checks present authorized trust/freshness/revocation/deployment context. Do not rewrite history on key rotation or expiry, and do not treat historical acceptance as perpetual permission. Missing archived material or unsupported evaluator versions are explicit replay limitations.

## Incremental evaluation (R39–R43)

Stage caches separately: parsing/canonical projections, prepared graph/obligations, verified inputs and time-sensitive decisions. Keys cover relevant subject/authority/profile/specification/binding/runner/adapter/trust/evaluator identities. Record validity boundaries for time-based inputs and invalidate on trust/configuration/authority changes. Do not use wall-clock buckets that permit stale success across a boundary.

Build reverse dependencies from source components and shared KMP source sets to targets, and from contracts/profiles/runners/adapters/trust to obligations. Handle renames/deletions and unclassified paths conservatively. `verify --affected` must use the result rather than simply loading a baseline. A cache/index miss expands or recomputes work; it does not remove obligations.

Batch tests by compatible runner/target/device/selection. Multiple requirements may reference one execution without counting it as independent evidence repeatedly. Bounded scheduling must respect device exclusivity, resources, cancellation and stable result ordering. Do not start a Gradle/Xcode process for every requirement or a native call for every displayed cell.

## Measurement

Measure cold preparation including canonicalization, derivation, evidence lookup, verification, full evaluation, serialization, storage contention/recovery and optional native overhead, plus warm/delta paths. Use realistic histories, profile combinations, cross-target scenarios, large matrices and host distributions. Record sample methodology, percentiles and peak memory on declared hardware. The baseline benchmark constants are not measured achievements from this conversation.

Keep a simple reference evaluation path. Property/differential tests compare optimized semantics to the reference for identical frozen inputs. Do not create a second independently evolving policy engine in the benchmark. Optimize bottlenecks only after correctness, with evidence of benefit and no relaxed validation.

========================================================================================
FILE: specs/TRUST_AND_RELEASE.md
========================================================================================

# Protected authority, verification and release decisions

## Threat and authority model (R23–R26, R64)

Candidate repository files, test code, runner/adapter output, imported evidence, logs, prose and MCP resources are untrusted claims. An approved typed graph validates local structure; it does not independently establish trust. A stored verified flag or deserialized receipt is not proof.

Trusted release authority is obtained independently of candidate-controlled changes. Protect policy, relevant contracts, requirement/target participation, evidence mappings and selections, waivers, trust configuration and the EQM evaluator used to grade the candidate. Deleting or reclassifying critical requirements/tests must be checked as possible weakening, not fewer obligations. Approved authority changes are versioned and explicit; protect the whole expectation chain rather than one file path.

The trust boundary must check signature validity, authorized identity/issuer, signer permissions, expected builder/producer, exact repository/source/build/artifact/configuration subject, approved execution context, and required time/revocation/verification material. Each mandatory input—evidence, release/candidate records, runtime facts—needs an explicit verification conclusion. Missing conclusions cannot disappear through filter_map/min aggregation.

A trust enum can remain display shorthand but does not replace independent acceptance dimensions. A claim cannot raise authority. Trusted test-only stand-ins stay inaccessible to production builds and configuration. Private constructors mitigate misuse by cooperating code, not malicious same-privilege execution.

## Cryptographic integration (R25)

Use a reviewed implementation and a provider-neutral internal verifier boundary. Sigstore bundle verification is the approved default CI integration direction, subject to inspecting exact library/tool support and pinning a currently audited implementation. Configure authorized identity/issuer, expected builder/subject, roots/material and algorithm policy explicitly. Do not invent real signer IDs, use arbitrary public signed artifacts as trusted EQM evidence, or disable claim checks to make an import pass.

Local deterministic cryptographic fixtures may be generated with test-only keys/material and clearly labeled. Production activation requires operator configuration and independent verification evidence. Default developer operation remains explicitly untrusted where appropriate. No implicit network acquisition; any needed retrieval is an authorized acquisition step, not a hidden evaluator action.

A persistent verification receipt binds exact bytes/digests, verifier identity, trust configuration, checked dimensions, time and supporting material. Reimport/replay reestablishes the required verification boundary. Preserve receipts for historical replay without treating them as permanently valid under future trust policy.

## Waiver contract (R29)

Waivers require explicit scope/approvers/reason/controls/start/expiry and protected provenance. Apply only to the precise obligations allowed by the normative rules. Report only actually contributing waivers, not every authored waiver in the graph. Agents must not create, widen, renew, or reinterpret waivers without human authority. Unknown trust/context and unstable evidence cannot be silently waived into satisfied evidence.

## Readiness, statements and authorization (R27–R28, R63)

Pre-release readiness binds a candidate subject before deployment. Post-deployment conformance evaluates actual deployed observations later. Runtime facts must be compared to expected exposure and exact subjects; mere document existence is not match. Separate lifecycle record types where required to avoid evidence/decision digest cycles.

Evaluation, optional signing, release authorization and deployment are distinct operations. A signed failure/unknown decision remains a signed failure/unknown decision. Unsigned reports say unsigned. Unknown never authorizes. Conditional release requires explicit protected acceptance of exact contributing deviations, not automatic interpretation of a waiver label as approval.

Authorization binds the decision, exact artifacts/participant subjects, channel/destination, policy/authority, allowed deviations and validity interval. The deployment system verifies this against what it actually promotes. EQM supplies validation/records, not a new deployment orchestrator. Artifact transformations after evaluation need an explicit trusted provenance relationship or new evaluation; the same commit is not enough.

Independent target release cadence requires a declared supported compatibility matrix. Do not assume all devices/apps/providers upgrade together. Scope a release to the combinations and participant roles the owner actually supports.

## Operational defaults

Keep production release enforcement disabled/shadowed until the supported-host, crypto, scope, exact-subject and deployment-consumption gates pass and an authorized operator approves enforcement. Do not leave an unconditional synthetic trust adapter behind a production feature flag. A rollback restores a known-good evaluator/authority or pauses promotion; it never trusts claims to preserve availability.

Missing production identities, product repositories, deployment routes or live verification material are explicit readiness blockers, not reasons to invent values. Implement generic contracts and local negative tests while preserving that distinction.
